newsitem.title: UK: BBC strengthens guidelines on sex and swearing.
newsitem.headline: BBC strengthens guidelines on sex and swearing.

text.p: The BBC on Wednesday published a new set of guidelines to its programme makers and gave them clearer advice on the use of strong language and the portrayal of sex.
The Producers' Guidelines, previously updated in 1993, were described by BBC Chairman Sir Christopher Bland as "the most comprehensive code of ethics in broadcasting".
The new edition stresses the importance of the nine o'clock "watershed" on television, the traditional cut-off point for more provocative material.
It also raises awareness of the offence caused by strong language, especially religious profanities and gives clearer guidance about the portrayal of sex.
"The BBC aims to set the highest editorial and ethical standards in programme-making," said Director-General John Birt.

"The Producers' Guidelines spell out our approach to the most difficult editorial issues, and provide detailed guidance which programme makers at all levels need to be aware of if we are to meet the expectations of our audiences," he added.
